name: mysterious-island-translations
work: Jules Verne, The Mysterious Island (L'Île mystérieuse, 1875)
description: Two English TRANSLATIONS of the opening chapter ('The Hurricane of 1865'), which begins in medias res with rapid balloon-crew dialogue. base = the Kingston translation.

white.excerpt: Part I, Chapter I 'The Hurricane of 1865' (between '^CHAPTER I\.' and '^CHAPTER II\.')

full.description: Whole-novel witnesses under full/ for scale collation testing — the LARGEST real pair in the corpus (a 3-part novel; ~195k / ~167k words, larger than 20,000 Leagues). Each witness's front matter (title / redactor's note / part heading) is wrapped in a <!-- no_collate --> region so only the novel body is collated.

witnesses.full/kingston.txt: ~195.0k words, from PG1268 (whole novel; front matter excluded before '^Chapter 1')
witnesses.full/white.txt: ~167.5k words, from PG8993 (whole novel; front matter excluded before '^CHAPTER I.')

full.collationResult: ~31,809 variants (25,381 substitutions, 4,192 deletions, 1,710 insertions, 526 moved); ~14.7 s (release) — the corpus's largest-scale timing test. Alignment: 25,919 shared points, 4.9% max drift, 98.0% monotonic — a clean diagonal; the collation holds end to end (the length difference is honest, not a mis-alignment).

notes: Excerpt pair yields ~388 variants (296 substitutions, 41 deletions, 28 insertions, 23 transpositions) — a demanding case; the opening dialogue is rendered quite differently by the two translators. The full/ witnesses are the corpus's LARGEST scale test — see the 'full' block.
